gaps.description: The trial lasts 14 days in the rules and 30 days in the reporting section.
gaps.recommendation: Keep the 14-day trial and correct the reporting section.
gaps.reasoning: Two lengths produce two different expiry dates and two different bills.

gaps.description: The charge is per active user, and active is never defined.
gaps.recommendation: Define an active user as one who signed in during the billed period.
gaps.reasoning: Counting every invited member and counting members who signed in are both readings, and they bill differently.

gaps.description: Two linked accounts carry two profiles, and no rule says which one wins.
gaps.recommendation: Ask the owner which directory is authoritative for the member profile.
gaps.reasoning: The choice is a policy about who owns member data, not something the document implies.

gaps.description: The text message service is assumed to reach every country the product is sold in.
gaps.recommendation: Confirm country coverage with the message provider before the sign-in work starts.
gaps.reasoning: Nobody has confirmed the coverage, and the fallback path changes if it is partial.

gaps.description: Stock is reserved immediately when an order is placed, and placed is not defined.
gaps.recommendation: Reserve at order submission, before payment authorization.
gaps.reasoning: Reserving at submission and reserving at payment are both readings, and they oversell differently.

gaps.description: Reading the warehouse endpoint on every product page view assumes a rate limit nobody confirmed.
gaps.recommendation: Confirm the warehouse rate limit, then decide between live reads and a cache.
gaps.reasoning: The design depends on a limit the warehouse team has not stated.

gaps.description: Reports are deleted after 90 days in the rules and kept for one year in the retention section.
gaps.recommendation: Keep one retention period and state it once.
gaps.reasoning: Two periods produce two different deletion jobs.

gaps.description: The report shows the figure the business reports externally, and no team owns that definition here.
gaps.recommendation: Ask the owner whether finance or sales owns the revenue definition.
gaps.reasoning: Only the owner can choose between two teams that define revenue differently.

gaps.description: Quiet hours run from 22:00 to 07:00 with no time zone.
gaps.recommendation: Apply quiet hours in the member's own time zone.
gaps.reasoning: Member local time and server time are both readings, and they hold different messages.

gaps.description: Notifications are turned off per channel in the rules and across every channel in the preferences section.
gaps.recommendation: Offer the per-channel switch and correct the preferences section.
gaps.reasoning: The two passages describe two different preference models.
